I need a detailed implementation plan for migrating the Boldteq marketing website from Webflow to Next.js 16.2.3. Here's the full context:

## Current Project State
- Project location: /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Boldteq/
- Next.js 16.2.3 already scaffolded with App Router, src/ directory
- Tailwind CSS 4 configured with shadcn/ui (base-nova style, OKLch colors)
- 9 shadcn/ui components installed: accordion, badge, button, card, dialog, input, separator, sheet, textarea
- framer-motion, embla-carousel-react, embla-carousel-autoplay installed
- next-sanity + @sanity/image-url installed for blog CMS
- posthog-js, @sentry/nextjs, next-sitemap installed
- Default layout.tsx with Geist fonts, default page.tsx (boilerplate)

## Pages to Build (from Webflow, published only)
1. **Homepage** (/) — Hero with typewriter effect, social proof logos, portfolio carousel, problem/solution cards, pricing preview, FAQ accordion, testimonials, newsletter signup, beta CTA
2. **How It Works** (/how-it-works) — 4-step process, features, risk mitigation, service model description
3. **Pricing** (/pricing) — 3-tier pricing table with monthly/quarterly/annual toggle, feature comparison table, ROI calculator (interactive sliders), custom plan section, beta CTA
4. **Our Work** (/our-works) — Portfolio grid with category filters (Shopify, WordPress), 19 projects with images, CTA
5. **Our Mission** (/our-mission) — Mission statement, values, delivery standards, company info
6. **Services: Website Development** (/services/website-development) — Pain points, services list (6 items), platforms (Shopify/WordPress), 4-step process, ideal clients
7. **Services: UI/UX Design** (/services/ui-ux-design) — Coming soon service page
8. **Services: Graphics Design** (/services/graphics-design) — Coming soon service page
9. **Blog** (/blog) — Blog listing with category filters, powered by Sanity CMS
10. **Blog Post Template** (/blog/[slug]) — Individual blog post, Sanity-driven
11. **Our Work Detail Pages** (/our-works/[slug]) — Individual portfolio case studies (9 detail pages: Dabble, Cinea, Dog & Crate, Junoone, Better Days, Lippy Oil, Frames for Prints, Sandscents, Repower Electric Supply)
12. **Careers** (/careers) — Hiring process, 5 job openings, culture pillars
13. **Contact** (/contact) — Contact form, email addresses, newsletter
14. **Book a Demo** (/book-a-demo) — Demo booking page
15. **Scope** (/scope) — Scope/services detail page
16. **Privacy Policy** (/privacy-policy) — Legal page
17. **Terms of Service** (/terms-of-service) — Legal page

## Design Style
- Primary: Dark navy (#092245, #082753)
- Accent: Cyan/turquoise gradients (#21cfff, #019ae6)
- Highlight: Yellow (#FFEB85)
- Neutral: White, light grays
- Clean sans-serif fonts
- Card-based layouts with shadows and border-radius
- Gradient overlays, icon illustrations
- Dark sections alternating with light

## Shared Components (appear on multiple pages)
- Navigation (sticky, with dropdown for Solutions and Resources)
- Footer (4-column links, social media, newsletter, "Designed with love from India")
- Newsletter signup section
- Beta CTA section (founding partner pricing)
- CTA banner ("Ready to Deliver This Level of Work Under Your Brand?")
- Chatwoot chat widget (script embed)
- Trustpilot widget (script embed)

## Key Interactions
- Typewriter effect on homepage hero (cycling text)
- Embla carousel for portfolio and testimonials
- Pricing toggle (monthly/quarterly/annual)
- ROI calculator with sliders
- FAQ accordion
- Scroll reveal animations (framer-motion)
- Mobile hamburger menu (sheet component)
- Category filter on portfolio and blog pages

## Technical Requirements
- Pure frontend / marketing site — NO auth, NO database (except Sanity for blog)
- Login button = external redirect to app URL
- Static generation (SSG) for all pages except blog (ISR for blog)
- Sanity CMS for blog posts and categories
- PostHog for analytics
- Sentry for error tracking
- next-sitemap for SEO
- All images optimized via next/image
- Fully responsive, mobile-first
- SEO metadata on every page (titles and descriptions already captured from Webflow)

## Constraints
- Stack A rules: No Vercel, no Stripe, no Prisma, no NextAuth, no CSS modules, no `any` types
- TypeScript strict mode
- pnpm only
- Tailwind 4 (no tailwind.config.js — use @theme in CSS)
- Host on Railway

## Plan Requirements
Please create a phased build plan with:
1. Project structure (all directories and files)
2. Phase 1: Foundation (layout, theme, shared components — nav, footer, newsletter, beta CTA)
3. Phase 2: Core pages (homepage, pricing, how-it-works, our-mission)
4. Phase 3: Service pages + portfolio (services/*, our-works, our-works/[slug])
5. Phase 4: Content pages (blog with Sanity, careers, contact, book-a-demo, scope, legal pages)
6. Phase 5: Polish (animations, SEO, analytics, sitemap, performance)
7. Phase 6: Deploy to Railway

For each phase, list exact files to create/modify and what each file contains.

19	The Metadata APIs can be used to define your application metadata for improved SEO and web shareability and include:
20	
21	1. [The static `metadata` object](#static-metadata)
22	2. [The dynamic `generateMetadata` function](#generated-metadata)
23	3. Special [file conventions](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) that can be used to add static or dynamically generated [favicons](#favicons) and [OG images](#static-open-graph-images).
24	
25	With all the options above, Next.js will automatically generate the relevant `<head>` tags for your page, which can be inspected in the browser's developer tools.
26	
27	The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are only supported in Server Components.
28	
29	## Default fields
30	
31	There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
32	
33	- The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
34	- The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
35	
36	```html
37	<meta charset="utf-8" />
38	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
39	```
40	
41	The other metadata fields can be defined with the `Metadata` object (for [static metadata](#static-metadata)) or the `generateMetadata` function (for [generated metadata](#generated-metadata)).
42	
43	## Static metadata
44	
45	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) from a static [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) or [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) file. For example, to add a title and description to the blog route:
46	
47	```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx" switcher
48	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
49	
50	export const metadata: Metadata = {
51	  title: 'My Blog',
52	  description: '...',
53	}
54	
55	export default function Layout() {}
56	```
57	
58	```jsx filename="app/blog/layout.js" switcher
59	export const metadata = {
60	  title: 'My Blog',
61	  description: '...',
62	}
63	
64	export default function Layout() {}
65	```
66	
67	You can view a full list of available options, in the [`generateMetadata` documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-fields).
68	
69	## Generated metadata
70	
71	You can use [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to `fetch` metadata that depends on data. For example, to fetch the title and description for a specific blog post:
72	
73	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher

## Key Risks and Mitigations

1. **Sanity schema not yet created**: The blog pages depend on a Sanity project with blog post and category schemas. This needs to be set up in the Sanity dashboard before Phase 4 blog work begins. Mitigation: create mock data to develop against, swap in real Sanity queries later.

2. **Image assets from Webflow**: All portfolio thumbnails, logos, and illustrations need to be exported from Webflow and placed in `public/images/`. This is a manual step that should start in Phase 1. Mitigation: use placeholder images during development.

3. **`@portabletext/react` not installed**: This package is needed for rendering Sanity blog content but is not currently in `package.json`. Must be installed before Phase 4 blog work: `pnpm add @portabletext/react`.

4. **Next.js 16 `params` as Promise**: All dynamic route pages (`[slug]`) must await `params`. This is a Next.js 15+ breaking change that must be followed consistently.

5. **Tailwind 4 syntax**: No `tailwind.config.js` exists. All theme customization goes in `globals.css` via `@theme inline`. Custom colors, spacing, etc. must be defined there, not in a config file.
